name: Numerical Weather Prediction Field Request Builder Nodes
description: Request-builder flow nodes for numerical-weather-prediction model fields in NOAA Open Data Dissemination's anonymous public buckets (NCEP GFS noaa-gfs-bdp-pds, GEFS noaa-gefs-pds), fetched message by message through each file's .idx inventory. plan turns a timer tick into the run's inventory requests, product by product and lead by lead, 16 per invocation, the rest yielded as backlog; select_messages reads the inventories and emits each lead-file's wanted messages as byte ranges (adjacent ones merged, each under 64 MiB), with a GRIB job per range, ONE LEAD-FILE PER INVOCATION, the rest yielded as backlog, so the parser holds one file's messages and storage-ingest receives one meta and one record stream at a time; publish_request turns a completed storage-ingest result plus the parser's ingest meta into the dataset-publication POST (nothing when nwp_publish_url is unset). Products are the world-clouds display's, chosen as its reference fetchers choose them: gfs-1p00-motion (winds and, early, heights at 1000-200 hPa), gefs-0p50-spread (the ensemble wind spread at every other point), gfs-0p50-clouds (instantaneous cloud cover, total and by layer), gfs-0p25-physics (2 m temperature/dew point, 10 m wind, boundary-layer height, CAPE, surface height, cloud layers, and the 21-level + tropopause profiles). Every request sets If-Modified-Since at the epoch so the host never turns a repeat inventory or range into an empty 304. Node CONFIG through plugin.getConfig: nwp_live_access, nwp_run, nwp_products, nwp_max_lead, nwp_lead_step, nwp_motion_heights_to, nwp_physics_leads, timeouts, nwp_publish_url. No credentials: capabilities none.

sequentialJustification.detail: Each method turns its control frames into request/job frames in one pass: plan reads the node config once and queues one inventory request per lead-file, select_messages parses the inventories and queues one entry per lead-file, publish_request pairs one result with one meta. The only state is the two queues, drained a batch per invocation as the compiled runtime resumes the yielded node; no worker pool and no thread.

methods.description: Timer tick -> the run's .idx inventory GETs, one per (product, lead), each with an inventory job naming the product, file URL, run and lead; 16 per invocation, the rest yielded as backlog and resumed without input. One status frame when live access is off. One tick per invocation (a surplus is refused as batched-input-frames).

wildcardJustification.detail: Cron timer tick frame produced by the flow runtime and consumed inside this flow only; it carries no payload of its own, so there is no SDS record to name.
hostcap/http-request request descriptor ({method,url,headers,timeoutMs,responseWire}) produced and consumed inside this flow; its shape is defined by the host http.request op, not by SDS.
Per-inventory job (product, file URL, run, lead) consumed by select_messages inside the same flow; never persisted.

outputPorts.description: One inventory job per request, in the same order.

wildcardJustification.detail: Cycle status ({skipped:<reason>} or {missing:[...]}) reported to the flow egress; diagnostics, never persisted as a record.

outputPorts.description: Why a cycle emitted nothing, or which files the listings lacked.

methods.description: Inventories + their jobs (paired by position) -> each lead-file's wanted messages (instantaneous fields of the product's variables and levels) as Range GETs, adjacent messages merged, each under 64 MiB, with a GRIB job per range. One lead-file per invocation; the node yields with the rest as backlog and the runtime resumes it without input. A missing inventory (a lead the run lacks) is reported on status; a count mismatch is refused.

wildcardJustification.detail: Per-inventory job emitted by plan inside the same flow; never persisted.
